title: Five Letters to Samuel Clarke
summary: The last controversy: Leibniz against the Newtonian divine Samuel Clarke, in the year before Leibniz's death — space and time as orders of things, the sensorium of God, the possibility of miracles, and the sufficient reason that Clarke's God does not need.
sourceNote: Seed text: G. M. Duncan, The Philosophical Works of Leibnitz (New Haven, 1908) — Leibniz's five papers of the correspondence; OCR transcription from the archive.org scan, US public domain.
editorialNote: Scanned-source OCR: minor transcription artifacts remain; a correction pass is scheduled. Clarke's five replies are in the companion work Dr. Clarke's Five Replies (from the 1717 Collection of Papers). Anchors §1–§5.
